samples.text:
The pie charts shows how much greenhouse gases was produced by different sectors in one country in 1990 and 2020.

In 1990, energy supply was the biggest sector with 36% of emissions. Industry was the second with 22%, and transport was 16%. Buildings produced 14%, agriculture 9% and waste only 3%, so waste was the smallest one. Energy supply and industry together made more than a half of all emissions.

In 2020, there was a lot of changes. Transport became the largest sector, it increased to 27%. Energy supply decreased a lot to 21%, but it was still the second biggest. Buildings went up to 18% and it was higher than industry, because industry fell down to 17%. Agriculture also rose to 13% and waste rose a little to 4%.

Overall, in 1990 energy supply produced the most emissions but in 2020 the transport was the main sector. Energy supply and industry went down, while all of other sectors increased during this thirty years.
samples.why: All figures reported accurately · overview present but only at the end · linking is adequate but mechanical · some repetition of vocabulary · several agreement, determiner and article errors that do not obscure meaning.

samples.text:
The pie charts compare the proportions of greenhouse gas emissions produced by six sectors in one country in 1990 and 2020.

Overall, energy supply was the largest source of emissions in 1990, but it had been overtaken by transport by 2020. While the shares of energy supply and industry declined, those of all the other sectors increased.

In 1990, energy supply accounted for more than a third of emissions (36%), followed by industry at 22% and transport at 16%. Buildings were responsible for 14%, and agriculture and waste contributed the smallest shares, at 9% and 3% respectively.

By 2020, the share of emissions from energy supply had fallen sharply to 21%, while industry's share had also dropped, to 17%. In contrast, transport saw a significant rise of 11 percentage points, reaching 27% and becoming the largest emitting sector. Buildings also increased their share to 18%, overtaking industry, and agriculture rose to 13%. Waste remained the smallest contributor, with only a slight increase to 4%. Consequently, the gap between the largest and smallest sectors became narrower over the period.
samples.why: Clear overview of the main changes · key features highlighted and supported with accurate figures · logical progression · varied linking devices · good vocabulary (emitting sector, contributor) · mostly error-free.

samples.text:
The charts break down one country's greenhouse gas emissions by sector in 1990 and 2020.

The most notable change over the thirty years was that transport replaced energy supply as the principal source of emissions. More generally, the shares attributable to energy supply and industry contracted, while every other sector accounted for a larger proportion by 2020.

In 1990, energy supply was responsible for 36% of emissions, well ahead of industry (22%) and transport (16%). Buildings contributed 14%, and agriculture and waste were comparatively minor sources, at 9% and 3% respectively.

By 2020, the picture had been transformed. The share generated by energy supply had dropped by 15 percentage points to 21%, and industry's contribution had also shrunk, to 17%. Transport, by contrast, rose from 16% to 27%, making it the largest single source of emissions. Buildings and agriculture both gained ground as well, reaching 18% and 13% respectively, so that buildings overtook industry. Waste remained the smallest category, edging up by just one point to 4%. As a result, emissions were spread more evenly across the main sectors at the end of the period than at the beginning.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected with a clear, well-placed overview · accurate figures used selectively with correct derived values · cohesion well managed · precise vocabulary · wide range of structures with no errors.
